propositions: Four AST guards pin scans to hardcoded single source files that no longer contain the constructs they police, yielding unconditional false-negative passes when the constructs move to sibling modules.

Guard F1 scans applier.py for invariants imports but the policed construct _repair_property migrated to apply_inbound.py; guard F2 scans runner.py for timeout primitives that relocated to structured_run.py and agent_call.py; guard F3 scans inbound_probe.py which is now a pure re-export facade while mechanics moved to adapters/jira/probe.py; guard F4 scans usage_log.py for colon-splitting calls that are now in config.split_provider_qualifier.

Each vacuous guard lacks an anti-vacuity assertion that would detect when the scanned population becomes empty, unlike proven non-vacuous guards that explicitly verify their scan targets still contain the policed construct.

Repair strategy: derive scan population from module import closure rather than hardcoded filenames, add landmark assertions ensuring scanned modules define specific constructs, add mutation tests that red when the construct is synthetically re-introduced at its real home.
